items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: I was playing with Thad Jones and Gil Evans and Joe Henderson and Kenny Dorham, and Clark Terry before I joined that band.

ctx.x: Because it really did bring jazz back to a lot of the public. It really paved the way for bands that really were much better than it, bands like Weather Report. But without Blood, Sweat & Tears to open that door I don’t know how long it would have been before a band like Weather Report could have been there. It really did a lot for bringing — it was the first thing that brought a little bit of jazz sound to the mass public in a long time. And for that I’m very proud that I was in the band because of that reason.…
That’s good. Was Blood, Sweat & Tears a difficult group as far as — some rock bands have personalities that constantly—
